# Reference Data

Expected output values for integration tests. Each JSON file contains both
C++ ground truth (from RecastNavigation CLI) and current Rust output.

## How values were generated

**C++ ground truth** was generated by running `RecastCLI` from the
[RecastNavigation](https://github.com/recastnavigation/recastnavigation)
repository with default parameters:

```bash
RecastCLI build --input test-data/meshes/nav_test.obj --output /tmp/nav_test.bin
RecastCLI find-path --mesh /tmp/nav_test.bin --start 5,0,5 --end 20,0,15
```

**Rust output** was generated by running `RecastBuilder::build_mesh()` and
`NavMeshQuery` with the same config parameters.

## Known divergences

The Rust port produces 10-12x more polygons than C++ for the same input
and config. Grid sizes and input counts match, so the divergence is in
the build pipeline (region building, contour extraction, or polygon
merging). This is tracked as a bug.

| Mesh | C++ Polys | Rust Polys | C++ Verts | Rust Verts |
|------|-----------|------------|-----------|------------|
| nav_test | 537 | 6683 | 1197 | 12867 |
| dungeon | 217 | 2747 | 452 | 5370 |
| bridge | 8 | 74 | 18 | 143 |

Multi-polygon pathfinding (`find_path` returning >1 polygon) does not
work in the Rust port due to a polygon link setup issue in
`build_from_recast`. The C++ CLI produces correct multi-waypoint paths.

## Integration test strategy

Tests validate the current Rust output to catch regressions. As pipeline
bugs are fixed, the expected values should converge toward the C++ ground
truth. Tests that compare against C++ values are marked `#[ignore]` until
the pipeline produces matching output.
